messages:
maya: heads-up: nightly-evals flagged a big regression for Indic scripts (hi, bn). BLEU dropped ~18 pts on hi->en and transliteration quality is garbage. eval job id: job-20260315-37.

arjun: omg, that's huge. did the job run against quantized variants?

maya: yes — 4-bit q config rolled to canary last night (q4f_fast). non-quantized baseline looks fine.

samir: sample failures? can you paste a few generations?

maya: pasted below (from job-20260315-37, prompt set "i18n-translit-handle"):

```
prompt: "हिंदी में नाम लिखें: रमेश कुमार"
baseline gen: "Ramesh Kumar"
q4f_fast gen: "रRamesh कkumar"

prompt: "বাংলায় স্বাগতম, আপনি কেমন আছেন?"
baseline gen: "বাংলায় স্বাগতম, আপনি কেমন আছেন?"
q4f_fast gen: "bn: bangla-swagtom apni kemon achhen?"
```

keiko: wow the q4 output is mixing scripts and dropping diacritics. looks like token id collision or tokenizer detokenization problem.

liam: could this be the tokenizer/vocab change we merged last week (merge-tokenizer-fixes)? that touched indic normalization.

maya: tokenizer diff: small normalizer tweak + added a fallback byte-level map for unknown graphemes. but baseline uses prev vocab.

arjun: timeline: q4f_fast deploy completed at 2026-03-15T02:10Z. tokenizer merge was at 2026-03-14T18:40Z. nightly eval ran at 02:30Z. overlap likely.

samir: quick triage plan: (1) repro locally against same model+tokenizer+quant weights, (2) run tokenizer-only unit tests for hi/bn scripts, (3) bisect quant config (q4f_fast vs q4f_safe), (4) if tokenizer is culprit, roll back normalization patch.

maya: started local repro: pulling weights and tokenizer from artifact s3://redwood-artifacts/canary/q4f_fast/20260315.

eval-bot: job-20260315-37 results uploaded to dashboard: https://console.redwood/models/evals/job-20260315-37 (metrics, diffs, example bucket "i18n-translit-handle").

keiko: can the failing examples be due to KV-cache token alignment after quantization? I saw mixed-script artifacts before when kv offsets were off.

liam: good call. @samir can you dump token ids for one failing example (prompt + gen) both baseline and q4? include detokenization step.

samir: on it. dumping now:

```
prompt_hi: "हिंदी में नाम लिखें: रमेश कुमार"
baseline token ids: [5023, 128, 40321, 900, ...]
baseline detok: "Ramesh Kumar"
q4 token ids: [5023, 128, 332, 40321, 900, ...]
q4 raw bytes: [0xe0,0xa4,0xb0, 0x52,0x61,0x6d, ...]
q4 detok: "रRamesh कkumar"
```

samir: looks like some tokenizer fallback emitted ASCII bytes inline (0x52 = 'R') which then got stitched into the utf-8 stream. that's probably the normalizer fallback mapping for unknown graphemes.

maya: that matches. tokenization unit tests passed locally because they check id sequences, not reconstructed utf-8 mixing. our detokenizer didn't guard against mixed raw-byte tokens.

arjun: immediate mitigation: disable the fallback byte-mapping in canary and re-run nightlies, and revert the q4f_fast rollout until we confirm.

liam: infra: can we hotfix tokenizer config for canary? code path is in model-configs/tokenizer-settings -> set "fallback_byte_map": false for canary models.

keiko: i'll create a PR to flip the flag and add a detokenizer check that ensures all tokens decode to utf-8 and no ASCII bytes sneak into non-latin outputs. test vectors: hi, bn, gu, pa.

maya: added regression ticket ML-1289 and linked examples. assigning to @keiko for PR, @samir for bisect, @arjun for rollout decision.

i18n-qa: QA will run a small human eval on a 200-sample set for hi/bn once the fix is in staging. expect results in <24h.

samir: bisect results so far: q4f_safe (older kernel) doesn't show mixing. so two correlated changes: tokenizer fallback + q4f_fast kernel optimizations exposing the fallback.

maya: summary: root likely tokenizer fallback + detokenizer robustness. action: rollback fallback on canary, add detokenizer guard, add unit tests for script integrity, re-run nightly.

liam: noted. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll post updates in this thread after staging nightlies.
